text.p: Italian bonds and futures swung higher on optimism over the chances of an official rate cut once preliminary inflation data have been released this week.

This week is filled with key events which will hold the market's attention, starting with the release of the first set of Italian CPI data for May tomorrow and an FOMC meeting to discuss U.S. interest rates.

"There's optimism for tomorrow and CPI with expectations of an imminent cut," a broker said. The June Btp LIFFE future held 70 bps up to 130.86 after touching 131.10 earlier, the highest point for the front month contract since February 25.
The February 2007 Btp ended 50 basis points up at 97.91 and the lira climbed to 980.45 before trickling back a little to 980.80/1.10.

Five sample Italian cities release consumer prices data after 1530 GMT on Tuesday and another six do so on Wednesday. Forecasts are for inflation at 1.5 percent year on year after 1.7 percent in April. At a Bank of Italy repurchase operation earlier the minimum rate fell to 6.78 percent, its lowest rate since 1982 when the repo tender was introduced.
All this led analysts to speculate whether the Bank of Italy might cut the 6.75 percent discount rate as early as Wednesday.
